# Dukanipāta (AN 2)

**ID:** AN 2
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Dukanipāta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dukanipāta* ("The Book of the Twos") is the second major division of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, organizing teachings and doctrinal principles into sets of two. Among its prominent discourses is the *Samacitta Sutta* (AN 2.35/36), delivered by Sāriputta to the "devas of tranquil mind," which addresses the residual rebirths awaiting practitioners at the first three stages of awakening (stream-enterer, once-returner, and non-returner) in either the sensual or higher realms [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. In another discourse, the Buddha designates his two chief disciples, Sāriputta and Mahāmoggallāna, as the exemplar and standard for all ordained monks to emulate (AN 2.131) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The collection also records Mahākaccāna's dialogue with the brahmin Kandarāyana (AN 2.38), in which the elder redefines seniority in the noble discipline, asserting that true elderhood stems not from advanced chronological age but from overcoming attachment to sensual pleasures [Nyanaponika et al. 2003].
